tx.t: Today I will explain how the human heart works. The heart has four chambers: two at the top, called atria, and two at the bottom, called ventricles.
At rest, the adult heart beats between sixty and one hundred times every minute. Over a day, that adds up to roughly one hundred thousand beats.
The heart pumps about five litres of blood around the body every minute. The heart of an adult weighs only about three hundred grams, and it is about the size of a clenched fist.
Regular exercise makes the heart stronger, so it can pump more blood with each beat.

tx.t: Let us begin with the early history of the bicycle. The first machine of this kind was built in eighteen seventeen by a German baron called Karl von Drais, and it had no pedals.

In the eighteen sixties, pedals were fixed to the front wheel, and the machines were nicknamed boneshakers because of their hard wheels. In the eighteen seventies, the penny-farthing had a huge front wheel, which made it fast but dangerous.

The safety bicycle of the eighteen eighties had two wheels of the same size and a chain driving the back wheel. In eighteen eighty-eight, John Dunlop introduced the air-filled tyre, which made riding far more comfortable.

tx.t: In this lecture I will describe the world's rainforests and why scientists want to protect them. Rainforests cover only about six per cent of the Earth's land surface.
However, they are home to more than half of all the plant and animal species on land. The Amazon is the largest rainforest, and it spreads across nine countries.
A rainforest has four main layers: the emergent layer, the canopy, the understorey and the forest floor. Most animals live in the canopy, where there is plenty of light and fruit.
Many modern medicines come from rainforest plants, and scientists believe thousands more are still unknown.

tx.t: Today I would like to talk about the history of the Olympic Games. The ancient Games began in seven hundred and seventy-six BC at Olympia in Greece.

They were held every four years for about twelve centuries, until they were banned in the late fourth century. The modern Games were revived in eighteen ninety-six in Athens, mainly through the efforts of a Frenchman, Pierre de Coubertin.
Women first took part in the Games in nineteen hundred, in Paris. The first Winter Games were held in nineteen twenty-four at Chamonix, in France.
Today, thousands of athletes from more than two hundred countries compete in the summer Games.

Its most unusual feature is a maker space with 3D printers, which is used mainly for local entrepreneurs.
The library is open ninety-four hours a week, and membership is free for everyone who lives in the city.
